label: Final copy step of length-3 sequences (t=5, outputting orig(2))
explanation: Fires almost exclusively in L=3 sequences (99.5% of activation mass), and there on the final step t=5 (copy step outputting the third original token, two steps after <DEL>); this single step fires in ~99.7% of L=3 sequences and holds 95% of the mass, with the strongest activations here. A weaker secondary activation occurs at t=4 in L=3 sequences (the step right after <DEL>, outputting orig(1)), holding about 4.5% of mass at low magnitude. Magnitude is largely uniform across token identities (no strong token dependence; slightly lower when sequences contain many digits). Never fires during the original phase or on the delimiter step, and is essentially silent for L>=4 (a handful of scattered weak activations).

issues: The claims hold on the test split. (L==3)&(t==5) scores P 0.997, R 0.777, F1 0.873, mass recall 0.953. On the dev split the unit is completely silent in the original and delimiter phases. L==3 holds 99.5% of the activation mass, and t=5 is active in 2598 of the roughly 2605 L=3 sequences.

The misses are not scattered noise. 747 of them are low-magnitude activations at t=4 in L=3 sequences (about 4.3-4.7% of the mass, concentrated in the bottom activation quartile). This is exactly the secondary mode the explanation describes. Adding these steps to the predicate (t>=4) drops test F1 to 0.759, so leaving them out is reasonable.
There are only 8 false positives at L=3, t=5. Most of them have orig(0) in {h, m}, which may be a minor token effect, but there are too few to matter.
The L>=4 activations are tiny (0.4% of the mass). Some cluster at t=11 (38 steps on dev), possibly the final step of L=6 sequences, but this is negligible.
Minor: I did not verify the claim that magnitude is slightly lower in sequences with many digits. It is peripheral.

Context note: the user's request mentioned features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5, but the computed task directed this review at features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store. I evaluated the latter as instructed.
